title: Work that lands in two places
eyebrow: Six points came back from the outside reader; all six are answered, checked and ticked off.

actions.fyi: Nothing is waiting on you. Override any decision below if you disagree with one.

content.label: What happened
content.lead: Some of our work does not live in this project at all — the board screen you read and the tools that build these pages are their own projects — and the board could not see finished work that had gone there.

rows: Work finished in the other project
stuck, could never be ticked off
ticked off, once the job says it goes there
could be ticked off on a change it never made
handed pointers it could not follow
told which project holds each one
refused until both halves are in

blocks.label: Unblocked
blocks.text: Four jobs whose work is in the board screen were stuck behind this and can now be ticked off.

blocks.label: Written down
blocks.text: The rule and the one gap it leaves are now in the board's own written rules, so the next person does not have to work it out.

content.label: The six points, and what was done

rows.title: A third place still asked the old question
rows.note: Already gone — the ruling of 13 August removed the only thing that asked it.

rows.title: The reader could not follow what it was given
rows.note: Every pointer now names the project holding it.

rows.title: Any job could be closed on the other project's work
rows.note: A job now says where its work goes, and is judged only against that.

rows.title: The written rule said the opposite of the code
rows.note: Rewritten, and the one gap left is written down.

rows.title: Nothing showed the change actually working
rows.note: Four checks run against live work, below.

rows.title: The same list was fetched twice for no reason

content.label: How we know it works
content.lead: Run against real work on the board, not against made-up examples.

rows: Finished only in the other project, and the job says it goes there
The same work, with the job no longer saying it goes there
The job says it goes somewhere this machine cannot see

blocks.label: Why the second row matters
blocks.text: Taking the job's own word away turns an accepted piece of work into a refused one, which is what shows the word is carrying it.

decisions.title: A job says where its work goes; the board never assumes
decisions.why: Trusting any project meant a page written about a piece of work counted as the work itself. A job that says nothing is judged here alone, so nothing on the board loosened.

decisions.title: One gap the reader wanted written down was closed instead
decisions.why: It cost two lines to fix. Writing down a fault we can remove in the same sitting is how a list of known faults grows without anything getting better.

decisions.title: The job's own finish line was rewritten
decisions.why: It named a file of checks that had already been deleted under your no-self-checks ruling, so it could never have been met as written.

decisions.title: Four jobs were marked as going to the board screen
decisions.why: Without it they would have gone from stuck to more stuck. A fifth was deliberately left out: the only thing it has over there is a page about the work, not the work.

next.if_nothing: Nothing waits on this one; the four stuck jobs are free to close.

steps.step: The four board-screen jobs stop being stuck and start closing
